question: Can passive-joint posture adjustment within the original joint ranges, together with contact load sharing, satisfy the root-plus-passive equilibrium that is infeasible at the nine retained placements?
hypothesis: Moving only the exactly-zero tendon-map DOFs (the passive tarsus chain) inside their original intervals may admit a contact-load sharing that balances the root plus passive rows; the unchanged saved poses are the fixed control.
units: Native MuJoCo model units, exactly as the existing source study; not animal measurements
controls: unchanged saved candidate pose re-derived as the first trial of every candidate
retained PR #19 placements, support matrices and passive-conflict receipts, byte-identical inputs
success_criterion: One declared trial whose saved witness replays root balance, passive-row balance and the original full 90-tendon static support; still a diagnostic placement, never standing or walking.
falsification: No declared posture reaching passive equilibrium in this grid rejects only this bounded single-DOF-plus-seeded search. Budget exhaustion, unbracketed trials and unresolved solver states are recorded separately and are never physical infeasibility.

parameters.search_dofs: exactly-zero tendon-map rows except the six free-root DOFs
parameters.control: unchanged saved candidate pose re-derived as the first trial
parameters.amended_from: FE-02-passive-posture-v1 pre-registration sized the call budget (640) below the declared trial list; this version only corrects that bound before any result was claimed
